summary: The simulation has a critical syntax error in NetworkDynamics.forward and a NameError in InteractionScheduler.forward that prevent execution. There are also robustness gaps (parameter clamping, adjacency guard), missing dict casting for parameters (location_mix), and incomplete metric coverage (purchase rate, contextual compliance, equity gap). Recent changes improved performance and stability (time caps, skip IO, homophily optimization, default calibrator), but introduced the syntax error and the variable name bug. The next iteration should fix these blockers, enhance robustness, and align metrics with the task spec.

critical_issues.issue: SyntaxError in NetworkDynamics.forward due to stray quote in default parameter
critical_issues.impact: Prevents the code from running at all; blocks any simulation or calibration.
critical_issues.solution: Fix the line to remove the stray quote in the default value for rewiring_rate.

critical_issues.issue: NameError in InteractionScheduler.forward: using undefined variable daily_contact_fraction
critical_issues.impact: Crashes at runtime when scheduling daily interactions, halting the simulation loop.
critical_issues.solution: Use the defined variable daily_fraction instead.

critical_issues.issue: InteractionScheduler lacks adjacency fallback and parameter clamping
critical_issues.impact: Can crash or misbehave when adjacency is None (e.g., edge cases) or when parameters are out of range, leading to unrealistic or unstable schedules.
critical_issues.solution: Add adj fallback and clamp daily_fraction and meeting_noise to [0,1]; ensure exogenous_rate is non-negative.

critical_issues.issue: ParameterManager._cast_value does not support dict parameters (e.g., location_mix) as JSON strings
critical_issues.impact: Overrides from CLI or JSON files for dict-typed parameters fail or are ignored, reducing configurability and experiment control.
critical_issues.solution: Extend _cast_value to parse dict dtype by attempting json.loads when the value is a string.

critical_issues.issue: SupplyChain._afford_prob may behave poorly for negative or zero income values
critical_issues.impact: Unbounded purchase burden can produce extreme probabilities and unrealistic purchasing dynamics for low-income agents.
critical_issues.solution: Clamp income to non-negative before computing burden.

model_improvements.current_approach: AdoptionAggregator computes adoption rate, transitions, and inequality index; buffers contextual adoption but does not persist it. Purchase attempts are tracked but purchase rate is not exposed as a per-capita metric. No enforcement events metric.
model_improvements.suggested_approach: Persist contextual adoption as a time series, compute and store purchase_rate_daily (attempts per capita), and add a simple enforcement proxy (e.g., counts of enforced-context mask consumption events or a dedicated enforcement counter).
model_improvements.expected_benefit: Better alignment with evaluation metrics: context_specific_compliance, purchase_rate, equity_gap, and potential enforcement_events.

model_improvements.current_approach: Uses a static disease_incidence_signal with simple risk_perception updates based on awareness.
model_improvements.suggested_approach: Add an EpidemiologicalSignal-like module or parameter to allow exogenous or endogenous time series for infection prevalence, and update risk_perception from that signal with noise and trend.
model_improvements.expected_benefit: More realistic dynamic adoption responses to epidemic phases; better fit to real-world trajectories.

model_improvements.current_approach: Enforcement signal is included in adoption logit but enforcement events are not counted.
model_improvements.suggested_approach: Track when agents in enforced contexts choose not to adopt and would face penalties or denial, and increment an enforcement_events counter.
model_improvements.expected_benefit: Enables reporting enforcement_events metric and analysis of policy impact and equity.

model_improvements.current_approach: ContextScheduler uses location_mix but cannot reliably accept dict overrides from CLI.
model_improvements.suggested_approach: Support dict parsing for location_mix in ParameterManager._cast_value to enable experiments with different context distributions.
model_improvements.expected_benefit: Improved experiment control and realism across varied mobility patterns.

code_improvements.modification: Remove stray quote in rewiring_rate default retrieval.
Replace daily_contact_fraction with daily_fraction, clamp parameters, and guard adjacency None.
code_improvements.reason: Prevents NameError and improves robustness of interaction scheduling.

code_improvements.modification: Add support for dtype == 'dict' by parsing JSON strings and ensuring dict type.
code_improvements.reason: Allows CLI/JSON overrides for dict parameters like location_mix.

code_improvements.modification: Clamp income to non-negative when computing burden.
code_improvements.reason: Prevents extreme or invalid probabilities for edge-case incomes.

code_improvements.modification: Expose supply.purchase_rate_daily and observable.contextual_adoption_rate to history; also persist inequality index.
code_improvements.reason: Aligns with evaluation metrics (purchase_rate, context_specific_compliance, equity_gap).

code_improvements.modification: Summarize equity_gap (e.g., mean over time) from history to metrics.
code_improvements.reason: Surface equity gap for evaluation and reporting.

data_alignment_suggestions.current_gap: Static disease_incidence_signal limits realistic phase transitions; adoption may plateau or rise unrealistically.
data_alignment_suggestions.suggestion: Feed a realistic prevalence time series (exogenous) and increase risk_perception_sensitivity during surges; calibrate intercept and policy weights with early-phase data.

data_alignment_suggestions.current_gap: Contextual adoption is computed but not persisted, preventing analysis.
data_alignment_suggestions.suggestion: Persist contextual series and compare against known context-specific compliance datasets (e.g., retail vs transit).

data_alignment_suggestions.current_gap: Inequality index is computed but not stored or summarized.
data_alignment_suggestions.suggestion: Record it in history and report mean/last values; calibrate purchase probabilities and enforcement penalties to match observed SES gaps.

data_alignment_suggestions.current_gap: Attempts tracked but per-capita rate not exposed.
data_alignment_suggestions.suggestion: Record purchase_rate_daily; validate against sales or distribution data if available.

Fix the NameError in InteractionScheduler.forward (use daily_fraction) and add adjacency guard and parameter clamps.

Clamp income in SupplyChain._afford_prob to non-negative.
Persist contextual adoption, purchase_rate_daily, and inequality index into Simulation.history; surface equity_gap summary in evaluate().
Plan integration of an epidemiological signal for dynamic risk feedback.

change_analysis.summary: Recent changes improved performance and stability (time caps for calibration, skip IO, optimized homophily rewiring, default calibrator set to none) and expanded features (context scheduler, supply chain, inequality metric). However, a syntax error and a variable name bug were introduced, blocking execution.
positive_impacts: Default calibrator set to 'none' and reduced budget prevents timeouts in constrained environments.
Added time budget guards for calibrators (logit_head, random_search, snpe) and counterfactual evaluation.
Optimized homophily rewiring via candidate sampling.
Added ContextScheduler and SupplyChain modules; AdoptionAggregator tracks stockouts and inequality.
negative_impacts: SyntaxError in NetworkDynamics.forward due to stray quote.
NameError in InteractionScheduler.forward due to incorrect variable name.
Contextual adoption and other metrics computed but not persisted to history, limiting evaluation.
suggestions: Fix the syntax and variable name issues immediately.
Add missing persistence for contextual and supply metrics.
Implement dict casting for location_mix to support experiments.
Plan a minimal EpidemiologicalSignal to drive risk perception for better realism.
